answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie voting weight to costly, non-transferable stake that gets slashed when an agent's attestations contradict consensus. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand stakes. Like pigment in paint, the capital stays fixed where it is put. Peers also draw random grading seats, so colluding clusters rarely meet, and any echo of fraud gets caught. New identities earn weight slowly, like a glacier, only after weeks of consistent honest work.
